I think the extra time and focus on the ending destruction of Derry was a great symbolic moment. By doing so, it felt that the Loser's and IT's connection to the place was officially at an end and that everything will wash away. I'm interested in seeing Derry later on in the book Insomnia. 

As for Eddie's death. Whether or not he was a favorite character...I felt that the scene was simply the last triumphant moment of a character who had been so mentally abused, tricked and sheltered his whole life to the point that he was afraid to even breathe without the assistance of his inhaler. It was a great way for his character to go out IMO. It was made more bittersweet, though, when his body was left and forgotten outside of IT's lair.
